abstract: We investigate the existence of static, spherically symmetric compact objects within the framework of symmetric teleparallel scalar-tensor gravity. This theory extends the Brans-Dicke and scalar-tensor models within the symmetric teleparallel formalism. We consider a nontrivial connection that allows for genuinely nontrivial solutions in the limit of General Relativity. The field equations admit a minisuperspace description and by applying the method of variational symmetries we construct the corresponding conservation laws in vacuum. The application of these conservation laws enables the reconstruction of analytic black-hole solutions. Finally, we study the interior structure of compact objects matched to an extremal Reissner-Nordström exterior and show that the symmetric teleparallel scalar-tensor theory supports the existence of viable astrophysical objects.
title: Compact Stars in Symmetric Teleparallel Scalar-Tensor Gravity
